column1: # The built-in licence identification table License identification reads, in order: the first row a declaration
# matches decides it, so the most specific rows come first - every LGPL and AGPL row before any GPL row, a licence's
# "-or-later" and "-only" rows before its plain version, a later version before an earlier one where one name is a
# prefix of the other, and the rows for a name that carries no version at all (GNU General Public License, BSD,
# Apache) last of all. An identifier may appear on more than one row; a bare declaration of it resolves to the first.
#   - the identifier matches a bare declaration ("MIT", "GPL-2.0-only") exactly, ignoring case;
#   - a name or a URL matches as a whole word inside "<declared name> <declared url>", lower-cased, with "licence"
#     read as "license"; a URL is written without its scheme, so http and https both match;
#   - the category is one of permissive, weak-copyleft, strong-copyleft, network-copyleft. Public-domain dedications
# An unversioned GNU licence name resolves to the earliest version "or later", which is what the licence grants when
# no version is named; any other unversioned name resolves to the version the name most often means today.
# Versioned names, identifiers and licence pages.
